did.abstract: This collection documents Frank Casier's, and his fellow local residents, campaigns against the Adirondack Park Agency (APA) Act and the actions of the Agency from the 1970s through the 1990s.
did.physloc: The materials are located onsite in the department.

bioghist.head: Biographical History
bioghist.p: Frank Casier and his wife Audrey were long-time residents of Saranac Lake in the Adirondack Region of New York. Beginning in 1976, Casier served as co-publisher of The Adirondack Defender, published in Defense of the People of the Adirondacks. He also founded the Adirondack Defense League in 1977.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The collection contains correspondence, letters to the editor, clippings, select issues of The Adirondack Defender, subject files, reports, flyers, political advertising, and video cassettes.

arrangement.head: Arrangement of the Collection
arrangement.p: The collection is unprocessed and is likely disorganized. Individual items may be difficult to find.

acqinfo.head: Acquisition Information
acqinfo.p: Frank, Audrey and David Casier donated the collection to the M.E. Grenander Department of Special Collections & Archives in 2015

accessrestrict.head: Access
accessrestrict.p: Access to this collection is restricted because it is unprocessed. Portions of the collection may contain recent administrative records and/or personally identifiable information. While it is likely that portions of the collection may be viewed, access must be managed by an archivist.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series consists of Frank Casier's activist work in which he organized and petitioned members of the community and legislation to dismantle the Adirondack Park Agency. Materials in this series consist of correspondences (petitioning to state officials, writing to fellow activists, and to fellow Adirondackers whose property rights may be at risk by The Adirondack Park Agency's land use regulations), notes from meetings held by the local government review board on The Adirondack Park Agency, plans for a civil lawsuit to be brought against The Adirondack Park Agency, protest flyers, letters to the editor, The Adirondack Park Agency Rules and Regulations, grievances of Frank Casier and fellow Adirondackers against the The Adirondack Park Agency, personal notes on The Adirondack Park Agency's private land use regulation, and newspaper clippings. This is the largest series in the Frank Casier Papers and is useful for researchers interested in understanding public reactions to land use regulations and reorganizing done by The Adirondack Park Agency to create the Adirondack Park.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series consists of select Adirondack Defender Issues (Vol. 1, No. 1, Vol. 1 No. 3-5, Vol 2. No. 1-4) published from 1976 to 1978. This series additionally contains drafts, newsletters, correspondences, and notes for upcoming issues of the newspaper. The Adirondack Defender was a small project, originally branching out of the Adirondack Defense League that Frank Casier and Tony D'Elia started and operated from Casier's home office. What started as letters to the editor to local newspapers grew to an independent Anti-APA political paper. Frank Casier and Tony D'Elia wrote articles for the paper and Melinda Hadley typed up the final product and acted as secretary. Newspapers were circulated for free to members of the mailing list or distributed in local businesses. The goal was to inform Adirondack residents about issues pertaining to the The Adirondack Park Agency and to inspire residents to join the action in petitioning New York government officials to "Abolish the APA". Most often it was used to discuss how public land use reconfiguration by The Adirondack Park Agency could potentially infringe on the private land of residents. This series would be useful for researchers interested in public reactions to The Adirondack Park Agency.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains correspondences to fellow Adirondackers about local community concerns and organizations, information on the formation of North Country Community College, notes on environmental concerns and legislature, newspaper clippings, publications, and other material that Frank Casier may have been interested in because of his activist work in the Adirondacks but did not pertain to The Adirondack Park Agency.
